title: Molecular Reactor: Dispersion Catalyst Balancing
description: The user operates a virtual chemical reactor where the DispersionTest model represents a prismatic dispersion chamber that splits energy into spectral catalyst beams, and the ShaderBall serves as a spherical reaction vessel. The user must balance reagent concentrations, temperature, and catalyst wavelengths across multiple coupled inputs while obeying conservation of mass and energy, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load DispersionTest.glb as a 'Dispersion Chamber' positioned at (-2,0,0) and ShaderBall.glb as a 'Reaction Vessel' at (2,0,0). Use PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,8) with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.4) and two directional lights. Build an HTML overlay UI panel with: (1) Three reagent sliders (Hydrogen 0-100, Oxygen 0-100, Nitrogen 0-100) whose sum must always equal 100 (conservation of mass — adjusting one auto-reduces others proportionally). (2) A temperature dial (200K-2000K) that affects a glowing emissive color on the ShaderBall material (blue=cold, red=hot) via linear interpolation. (3) Three wavelength toggle buttons (Red/Green/Blue catalyst beams) that create visible THREE.Line objects from the DispersionTest model to the ShaderBall, each colored accordingly. At least one beam must always be active (conservation of energy). (4) A pressure gauge (1-10 atm) that scales the ShaderBall uniformly between 0.8x and 1.5x. (5) An Undo/Redo button pair tracking all slider, toggle, and dial changes in a history stack (minimum 20 states). The DispersionTest model should slowly rotate on its Y-axis (0.005 rad/frame). When all three beams are active and temperature exceeds 1500K, trigger a 'reaction complete' particle burst using 200 small sphere geometries emitting outward from the ShaderBall with randomized velocities, fading over 2 seconds. Display a real-time status panel showing current reagent percentages, temperature, pressure, active beams count, and reaction status. Each interaction step (slider change, toggle, dial adjustment) should produce a visible immediate effect on the 3D scene. Ensure all coupled constraints update in real-time without allowing invalid states.
